source.reported_origin: Mooncake P/D disaggregation lacked support for Qwen3.5-style hybrid full-attention and GDN state groups. During review, DeepSeek V4 Flash exposed a second layout failure: standalone GSM8K accuracy was about 0.9507 while the pre-existing 1P1D Mooncake path produced about 0.0485. Investigation separated physical row stride from effective MLA payload and expanded the change to shared storage registration, per-group blocks, null-state placeholders, and recurrent-state prompt boundaries.

behaviors: transfer regions preserve physical row stride, effective payload length, layer order, and KV group identity
blocks-first full attention splits K and V while GDN, MLA, and sliding-window MLA remain whole payload regions
metadata round-trips all layout fields and rejects incompatible producer/consumer groups
hybrid remote prefill and decode preserve the recurrent-state final-token boundary for token IDs and prompt embeddings
pure attention and NIXL remote-prefill behavior remains compatible
logical block expansion applies to attention groups but not GDN state slots
hybrid registration exposes both FA and GDN regions and deduplicates shared backing storage
padded MLA and sliding-window MLA address by physical stride but copy only effective payload bytes
per-group transfer planning skips null placeholders, trims partial hits, reports group mismatches, and keeps empty state groups empty
verifier_contract.collection_integrity: JUnit must contain at least 23 passing, unique, non-skipped cases including MLA stride/payload, per-group/null planning, recurrent prompt handling, and shared-storage registration.

real_lifecycle_boundary.kind: real Mooncake registration and transfer planning over CPU tensors with an in-memory byte-copy transport engine
real_lifecycle_boundary.entrypoint: producer register_kv_caches -> transfer-region alignment -> _build_transfer_params -> batch_transfer_sync_write -> decoder tensors
real_lifecycle_boundary.limitation: The CPU image does not load the optional native Mooncake RDMA engine. The verifier executes production registration, region alignment, group-aware address planning, and actual pointer-based byte copies through a deterministic in-memory transport replacement; it does not claim network or GPU DMA coverage.
